GHOST-TEST ANALYSIS (rule 26), per it-block, delete-the-feature test:

omniauth spec it#1 ('calls from_omniauth with keywords and string-key tracking'): FALSIFIABLE. `have_received(:from_omniauth).with(auth: anything, created_via: 'created_via_weworkremotely_referral', partner_source: 'wwr', utm_source: 'SomeRawValue', utm_campaign: 'Camp01', utm_data: {'utm_medium'=>'cpc'}, internal_ref: 'ref-99')` is an exact-arg keyword matcher. Ruby 3.1.6 + rspec-mocks 3.13.7 distinguish kw-args from a positional hash, so reverting to the pre-feature positional call `from_omniauth(oauth_data, created_via_value, partner_param)` fails the matcher (and would ArgumentError since keywords are now required). Dropping any one utm key fails the exact match. created_via value is derived: get_created_via({partner:'wwr'}) -> mapping[:wwr]='created_via_weworkremotely_referral', so the assertion tests real derivation, not a constant. redirect_to("#{Variables::AtsRootUrl}/") matches controller line 37 exactly.

omniauth spec it#2 (nil case): FALSIFIABLE. No session tracking -> session.delete(:oauth_tracking)||{} -> merged={} -> all four values nil, created_via='created_via_signup'. If the controller fabricated a fallback for an absent value the exact-nil matcher fails.

DEVISE MAPPING (rule 30): omniauth spec has BOTH `include Devise::Test::ControllerHelpers` (line 15) AND `@request.env['devise.mapping'] = Devise.mappings[:api_v1_user]` (line 35, before block). Mapping name :api_v1_user is CORRECT (devise_for :users nested under api/v1 namespace -> mapping api_v1_user; confirmed by `devise_scope :api_v1_user` at routes.rb:126). assert_is_devise_resource! (prepend_before_action) reads env['devise.mapping'] before the action and passes. Controller line 5 re-sets env['devise.mapping']=Devise.mappings[:user] (nil, pre-existing, unchanged in diff) AFTER the prepend runs and does NOT break sign_in: Devise sign_in(user) resolves scope via Devise::Mapping.find_scope!(User_instance) which matches by class -> :api_v1_user, independent of env['devise.mapping']. So dispatch succeeds. confirmations spec correctly OMITS the mapping: Hire::ConfirmationsController < Hire::BaseController < ApplicationController < ActionController::Base -- NOT a DeviseController, so no assert_is_devise_resource!; no mapping needed. Route 'confirmations#show' exists under `scope module: :hire` (routes.rb:577); no global authenticate_user! before_action in ApplicationController or Hire::BaseController (only skip_before_action :track_ahoy_visit), so get :show dispatches unauthenticated as in production.

All three jobs exist (app/jobs/posthog_identify_job.rb, posthog_track_job.rb, org_owner_update_job.rb) so no NameError.

user_from_omniauth_spec, per it-block (calls REAL from_omniauth):
it#1 ('four values stored raw'): FALSIFIABLE. Input partner_source:'WWR' -> expects 'wwr' (from_omniauth line 388 partner_source&.downcase), proving the RAW-vs-downcase distinction is actually exercised: utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref expected verbatim ('SomeRawValue' not downcased) while partner_source is downcased. utm_data eq({'utm_medium'=>'cpc'}) with string keys matches the in-memory assigned hash (first_or_create returns the built object, not reloaded) and also survives a jsonb round-trip. Dropping any assignment (line 389-392) makes the value nil and fails.
it#2 ('nil when omitted'): FALSIFIABLE. Defaults nil -> columns nil. A `|| ''`-style fallback would fail the be_nil assertions.
it#3 ('does not assign to existing user'): FALSIFIABLE and is the key structural pin -- pre-creates the same-email user (no utm), calls from_omniauth with 'ShouldNotStick' values, asserts not_to change(User,:count) (first_or_create finds existing, block skipped) and all four columns stay nil. If assignment moved outside the first_or_create block (i.e., assigned to existing users too) this fails.
it#4 ('requires auth and created_via'): REAL. Ruby required keyword args -> ArgumentError when omitted. Adding defaults (auth: nil) would instead NoMethodError on auth.info.email, still failing the raise_error(ArgumentError) expectation, so the test genuinely pins the required-keyword contract.

confirmations_controller_spec, per it-block:

Devise stores the confirmation_token RAW in the column (generate_confirmation_token assigns self.confirmation_token = @raw_confirmation_token = Devise.friendly_token), so confirm_by_token(user.confirmation_token) confirms; no pending invite for the email -> user.errors.blank? -> redirect_to '/auth?email_confirmed=true' (controller line 18, byte-identical, bare URL with NO id/email).
